diagnostics.message: aws_cloudwatch_event_target.dispatcher wires the workflow_job rule to the dispatcher Lambda, but does not depend on aws_lambda_permission.allow_cloudwatch_to_call_lambda. The rule/target can be created and events can fire before EventBridge is granted lambda:InvokeFunction, so early invocations fail. The target should be created only after the permission exists (e.g. a bare depends_on). The provider docs note that a Lambda permission must be set up for EventBridge to invoke the function.

When VPC mode is enabled, aws_lambda_function.webhook is created with a vpc_config and needs ec2 ENI permissions from the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole policy, but it only references aws_iam_role.webhook_lambda.arn and not aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role. If the function is created before the attachment, ENI provisioning fails ("role does not have permissions to call CreateNetworkInterface"). The function should depend on the attachment.

When VPC mode is enabled, aws_lambda_function.dispatcher is created with a vpc_config and needs ec2 ENI permissions from the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole policy, but it only references aws_iam_role.dispatcher_lambda.arn and not aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.dispatcher_vpc_execution_role. If the function is created before the attachment, ENI provisioning fails. The function should depend on the attachment.
